evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:412-415 (initializeAuth) — cold-boot restores the session as authenticated whenever BOTH a stored user and a stored access token exist: `if (storedUser && accessToken) { setUser(storedUser); }`. No expiry check is performed on the access token despite the inline comment at L413-414 explicitly flagging the gap ('Validate the token is not expired (basic check)' / 'In production, we might verify with the server').

The cold-boot refresh branch at AuthContext.tsx:416 (`else if (refreshTokenValue)`) only runs when the access token is ABSENT. A returning user with a still-present but EXPIRED access token (and a valid refresh token) therefore skips refresh entirely and is shown an authenticated UI backed by a dead token.

A `decodeJwtPayload` helper already exists in this same file (AuthContext.tsx:220-232) and returns the JWT `exp` claim, so a cheap client-side expiry check is readily available but unused on the init path. Fix: if the stored access token's `exp` is in the past, fall through to the `refreshTokenValue` branch instead of calling setUser(storedUser).

Impact is compounded by the absence of any silent refresh-on-401 interceptor (see companion finding code-review-ppt-web-core-api-onunauthorized-unwired): with no auto-recovery, the expired-token session does not self-heal and the user sees failing requests until a manual re-login.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:219-221 — the hand-rolled axios response interceptor handles 401 via `if (error.response?.status === 401 && onUnauthorizedCallback) { onUnauthorizedCallback(); }`, reading a module-level `onUnauthorizedCallback` (declared api.ts:180, assigned only inside configureApiClient at api.ts:196).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:337 is the ONLY production call site of configureApiClient and it passes `configureApiClient({ getToken: getAccessToken })` with NO `onUnauthorized`. `onUnauthorizedCallback` therefore stays undefined at runtime and the 401 branch in api.ts is dead — a 401 from this client neither refreshes the session nor logs the user out; it just rejects with a transformed ApiError. (grep confirms no other non-test configureApiClient call.)

The behavior the missing callback should provide is explicitly documented as present by consumers: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts:19 and frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts:10 both describe the shared client as doing '401 -> onUnauthorized'. That contract is not wired, so those feature endpoints silently fail on session expiry with no recovery.

There is also no response-side refresh interceptor on the generated @ppt/api-client: registerAuthInterceptors (packages/api-client/src/auth/interceptors.ts:36-51, invoked at apps/ppt-web/src/main.tsx:26) registers only a REQUEST interceptor that injects Authorization + X-Tenant-ID headers. So neither client performs silent refresh-on-401 app-wide. Fix: pass an onUnauthorized handler (trigger AuthContext.refreshToken with single-flight, fall back to logout) at the configureApiClient call site, or remove the dead branch + misleading hook comments.
